bibl.title: Worlds Apart Trading Together: The Organisation of Long-Distance Trade between Rome and India in Antiquity
bibl.seg: Kasper Grønlund Evers, Worlds Apart Trading Together: The Organisation of Long-Distance Trade between Rome and India in Antiquity = Archaeopress Roman Archaeology. 32.
Oxford, Archaeopress, 2017, viii-213 pp., figg. ISBN 978-1-78491-742-5. £30.

C.R. par Jeremy Simmons, BMCRev < https://bmcr.brynmawr.edu/2018/2018.09.59 >. - Roberta Tomber, JRA 31 (2018) pp. 948-952 [concerne aussi: Rajan Gurukkal, Rethinking Classical Indo-Roman Trade: Political Economy of Eastern Mediterranean Exchange Relations (New Delhi, 2016)].
bibl.note: Introduction. - 1. What's in a name? A brief historiography of Indo-Roman trade. - 2. Ancient history "from below". Theoretical perspectives. - 3. Turning the tables on Indo-Roman trade. - 4. The invisible hand of Roman organisations. - 5. Demand and supply in Rome and the provinces. - 6. The modus operandi of Roman long-distance trade. - 7. Towards a wider world of trade in the ancient Indian Ocean. - 8. The invisible hand of Indian organisations. - Conclusion: Worlds apart trading together. - Maps. Bibliography.
